status: PRODUCTION DRIVING BASE - Selena Navarro. v1. QA gate PASS, all rows. Not yet used downstream.
purpose: Reusable driving video for LatentSync. Derived from the usable arc of her approved motion base by RE-ORDERING its frames only. Built once; reused across Selena's 42 courses and every application video she presents.

derived_from.unchanged: The approved motion base is untouched and verified byte-identical after this build.
derived_from.chain: approved reference presenter-3-selena-navarro-master.png (1672x941, sha256 fbbd1f22..., byte-identical throughout) -> production still presenter-3-selena-navarro-production-still-1920x1080.png (sha256 bbf914e2...) -> KIE kling/v2-1-pro take 3 + ffmpeg exposure correction -> this base.

method.cost: $0.00 - ffmpeg only. No new generation, no Kling call, no TTS, no interpolation, no synthetic frames. No paid API was called at any point in this build or its QA.
method.pixels: Every output frame is a copy of a decoded frame of the approved motion base. Only the ORDER changes. No filtering, no colour work, no scaling, no upscale.
method.source_region: Frames 1-51 ONLY - the arc around the clip's re-enterable blink. All 51 frames of the window are used.
method.walk: A CONTINUOUS walk along the source frame index, every step +-1, so no move contains a cut; a change of direction reads as the head settling. Wander legs are >=10 frames inside each pool.
method.structure: The blink at 23-27 splits the window into two pools, L=[1,22] and U=[28,51], and the walk crosses between them ASYMMETRICALLY: L->U IS THE BLINK ITSELF, walked forward 22 -> 23,24,25,26,27 -> 28, needing no join at all; U->L is the one join, skipping backwards over the blink. Exactly one join per blink.
method.blinks: The motion base contains exactly TWO blinks, located by eye on motion-TRACKED eye crops of all 121 frames - a fixed box measures the head drift (up to 21 px vertically) rather than the eyelid. Blink 1 is frames 23-27, blink 2 frames 52-56. Only blink 1 is used; see why_window_1_51.
method.joins: 31 joins, one per blink, cycling the four cheapest backward pairs over blink 1: 28->22 (3.317), 29->22 (3.686), 28->21 (4.128), 29->21 (4.154). Varied so the frames around a blink are never the same twice.
method.no_photometric_correction: Take 3 was already exposure-corrected before acceptance (2.59% -> 0.12% peak). Across frames 1-51 the per-channel mean spread measures 0.23/255 (~0.24%), far below the 1.182 RMS the source moves between two consecutive frames inside the window. Correcting it would rewrite every pixel to chase a difference smaller than the clip's own frame-to-frame noise. Left alone; every output frame stays a bit-exact copy.
method.reproducible: Fixed-seed LCG (20260820). Same script + same source = same .seq.
method.encode: libx264 -preset slow -crf 12 -pix_fmt yuv420p -an -movflags +faststart (same settings as Diane's and Curtis's bases)

why_window_1_51.finding: The motion base is two disconnected halves. Frames 51-80 carry a large head move (the head rises ~21 px and returns) and 81-121 settle out of it - the most movement in the clip - and blink 2 sits at its start. A blink may only ever be walked FORWARD, so reaching that half means joining back down across blink 2.
why_window_1_51.measured: The cheapest upper->lower join anywhere in the clip is 62->51 at 10.975 whole-frame RMS. The source's own blink-free motion is 5 frames median 5.340 / max 10.721 and 6 frames median 5.886 / max 11.586 - so that join is a SIX-frame jump, at the extreme tail of what the source ever does. It would read as a cut.
why_window_1_51.contrast: Around blink 1 the head is calm and the same joins price at 3.317-4.154 - below the source's own 2-frame MAXIMUM inside the window (4.873). Each join is a smaller visual step than one the source already takes between two frames two apart.
why_window_1_51.second_benefit: Frames 1-51 are also the expression-consistent half. The tracked lip-aperture proxy runs 75-85 there and 56-60 across frames 57-121 (the closed-lip smile relaxing to neutral, accepted as non-blocking in the motion base's own sidecar). Building inside one half means the delivered base never oscillates between the two expressions.
why_window_1_51.cost_of_the_choice: 51 of the clip's 121 frames are used. The larger head excursion in frames 51-121 is not reachable without a visible cut and is therefore not used. Recorded as a deliberate, measured decision - not an oversight.
why_window_1_51.if_more_movement_is_ever_wanted: It needs a new motion base generated with a movement-positive prompt that still keeps the lips closed AND places a blink inside the moving passage (~$0.25-0.50 a draw, a new approval under locked pipeline rule 7). Nothing in this build forecloses that; this base would simply be rebuilt for $0.00 from the new take.

blink_schedule.note: Irregular by design, with clustered doubles. All 31 traversals are the same blink (frames 23-27) - the clip's only re-enterable one. Diane's shipped base does the same with her single blink; Curtis's alternates two because take 2 had two usable ones.
blink_schedule.source_rate_for_comparison: The motion base itself blinks at 23.8/min (2 blinks in 5.04 s). Diane's shipped driving base is 13.25/min, her delivered v4 segments 11-15/min, and Curtis's production driving base 12.67/min - the last of which is also below the 13/min floor and was accepted.
blink_schedule.rate_assessment: 12.97/min against the established 13-20/min target - ACCEPTED as a documented non-blocking tolerance, not a numeric pass. See qa_gate.accepted_tolerances.blink_rate.

qa_gate.verdict: PASS. Blink INTEGRITY and every other row pass outright. The blink RATE is recorded as a documented non-blocking tolerance, not as a literal numeric pass - see rows.blink_validity and accepted_tolerances.blink_rate.
qa_gate.run_on: The delivered file. Frame fidelity and order were proven on ALL 3442 delivered frames by per-frame PSNR against the exact planned frames; per-frame metrics are then computed on the source frames indexed by the delivered .seq, and cross-checked directly on 238 + 244 decoded delivered frames (joins, blinks, camera lock, photometrics, an unbiased 122-pair step sample).

rows.audio: PASS - no audio stream at all.
rows.source_containment: PASS - the build asserts min/max source frame inside 1-51; actual range used 1..51, all 51 distinct frames. No frame from the disconnected upper half can enter the sequence.
rows.frame_fidelity: PASS - PSNR against the exact re-ordered source pixels across ALL 3442 frames: mean 52.97 dB (Y 52.16), per-frame minimum 49.65 dB. Curtis measured 53.79 dB, Diane 55.64 dB. This also proves every output frame is the planned source frame.
rows.camera_lock: PASS - best-fit zoom against delivered frame 1 is 1.000x at output frames 821, 1681, 2519 and 3442, measured on a PRESENTER-FREE region (0,40,840,860). A 2D registration search +/-24 px on the wall/logo region returns dx=0, dy=0 at all four, with no offset improving the fit. Background drift over the whole 143.4 s across five presenter-free regions: wall/logo 2.610, desk 2.248, shelf 2.802, art 3.030, window/city 3.186 /255 max. The motion base's own camera-lock row measured 4.009 mean / 4.436 max, so the base sits below its source's generative noise floor.
rows.lips_sealed: PASS - tracked lip-aperture floor across every delivered frame is 75.1/255 (median 80.25, max 85.63). The gate threshold is ~48 and an exposed oral cavity reads under 30, so the floor clears it by 27 points. Confirmed by eye on a tracked mouth contact sheet: lips together, no separation, no teeth, in all 51 distinct frames. Unlike Curtis there was no open-mouth defect to design around - all 121 source frames are sealed.
rows.natural_head_face_motion: PASS - tracked head position across the delivered base spans dx -2..+1 and dy 0..+8 px, RMS 1.60 px about the mean. Delivered face-region consecutive motion: mean 2.590, max 7.442 /255, against the source's OWN consecutive face motion inside the window of mean 3.701, max 11.573 - i.e. always within, never exceeding, the motion the source itself makes. For context, Diane's shipped v4 base carries a known limitation of 0.42 px head RMS; this base moves 3.8x that. 206 legs, median 14 frames (0.58 s), mean 16.6, max 45; direction changes average one per 19.8 frames (0.82 s).
rows.blink_validity: PASS on integrity; rate accepted on tolerance. INTEGRITY - PASS outright: 31 complete in-order forward runs of source frames 23-27, ZERO reversed blinks, ZERO blinks entered across a join, ZERO orphaned or partial blink frames, and no join lands on a blink frame. Audited straight off the delivered .seq and confirmed by eye on decoded delivered frames 58-68: open, open, open, closing, shut, shut, opening, open, open, open, open. RATE - 31 blinks / 143.417 s = 12.97 blinks/min, gaps 1.542-8.583 s, irregular. The established target is 13-20/min (docs/VIDEO_1_GENERATION_CONFIGS.md, 'Base QA gate'). 12.97 is 0.03/min under the floor - it rounds to 13 and is 0.23% below it. ACCEPTED as a documented non-blocking tolerance, NOT scored as a literal numeric 13-20 pass. See accepted_tolerances.blink_rate for the basis.
rows.continuity_and_joins: PASS - zero non-continuous steps outside the 31 declared joins across all 3441 transitions. Ordinary step RMS: median 0.889, p99 2.913, max 2.976 - the max is exactly the source's own 1-frame maximum inside the window, as it must be, since every ordinary step IS a source step. The 31 joins run 3.317-4.154 (median 3.686), which sits between the window's own 2-frame median (1.851) and 3-frame median (2.498) and BELOW its 2-frame maximum (4.873). Verified by eye at 2x on the cheapest and the most expensive join: both read as continuous motion, not as a cut.
rows.photometric_stability: PASS - across decoded delivered frames the channel-mean spread is R 0.242, G 0.134, B 0.268 /255 and the maximum channel shift is 0.386%. No correction applied or needed.
rows.loop_fit: PASS - first-vs-last whole-frame gap 1.575 /255 measured on the delivered file (Curtis 1.459, Diane 4.51). Relevant only if a single call ever exceeds 143.417 s and pingpong triggers - which the length rationale below is designed to prevent.
rows.source_integrity: PASS - after the build, re-checksummed: motion base 6fd0f857... unchanged, take 3 corrected 6fd0f857... unchanged, take 3 raw 0f690852... unchanged, production still bbf914e2... unchanged, approved master fbbd1f22... unchanged. Take 1, take 2 REJECTED and the selected voice master were also re-checksummed and are unchanged.

direct_verification.unbiased_step_sample: 122 consecutive delivered pairs spread evenly across the base: delivered median 0.835 / max 2.982 against planned median 0.849 / max 2.976, max per-pair difference 0.219 (h264 noise).
direct_verification.joins_on_delivered: All 31 joins measured directly on decoded delivered frames: 3.294-4.154, median 3.703. Maximum difference from the planned value 0.0235.
direct_verification.note: An earlier pass measured camera lock on a probe region that included the presenter and a 'shelf' region overlapping her hair; both were re-cut presenter-free before the figures above were taken. The contaminated readings measured her head movement, not the camera.

accepted_minor.measured: 3 frames = 0.125 s each, out of 206 legs (1.0%). Each covers 3 frames of source travel, inside the source's own 3-frame motion (window median 2.498, max 6.377).
accepted_minor.status: ACCEPTED - these are the leftover-slack micro-legs the min_leg logic minimises but cannot always eliminate. At 0.125 s they are not perceptible, and every frame in them is still a source frame reached by +-1 steps.

blink_rate.measured: 31 blinks / 143.417 s = 12.97 blinks/min; gaps 1.542-8.583 s, irregular.
blink_rate.target: 13-20/min, irregular - docs/VIDEO_1_GENERATION_CONFIGS.md, 'Base QA gate - free, ffmpeg, before ANY lip-sync spend'.
blink_rate.shortfall: 0.03 blinks/min below the floor; 0.23%. Rounds to 13/min at the precision the target is stated in.
blink_rate.status: ACCEPTED - documented non-blocking tolerance. This is deliberately NOT recorded as a numeric 13-20 PASS.
basis: The shortfall is inside the rounding of the target as written. One additional blink would put the base at 13.39/min; one fewer at 12.55/min - the schedule cannot be tuned finer than ~0.42/min at this length, so 12.97 is the closest attainable value at or below 13.

PRECEDENT: both shipped predecessors sit in the same place and were accepted. Curtis's production driving base is 12.67/min and Diane's delivered claims-01 v4 measures 12.9/min (11-15/min per segment). Diane's earlier shipped base was 13.3/min.
The failure mode this target exists to catch is the opposite one: the first Diane base shipped at 47.6/min and had to be rebuilt. A rate marginally under the floor is not that defect.
Blink integrity - the part that is structurally verifiable - passes outright and is unaffected.

The gate as written is the MOTION-base gate, applied to a generated take where the rate is whatever the model produced. On a driving base the rate is a free parameter set by the build schedule, so this is a tuning value, not a property of an accepted generation.
blink_rate.how_to_change_it_if_ever_required: Add one gap to GAPS in the build script and re-run: $0.00, no generation, no new approval. The existing frames stay identical and every other measured row is unaffected. Not done here - it was not judged worth reissuing a QA-passed asset over 0.03 blinks/min.
blink_rate.ruled_on: Recorded 2026-08-20 at Luis's direction. Non-blocking; not an open QA item.

length_rationale.headroom: 19.5% above the ~120 s chunk ceiling in docs/COST_OPTIMIZATION_267.md 6.2. Curtis's base carries 18.4%.
length_rationale.why_it_matters: The base must be longer than the longest single LatentSync call so loop_mode never triggers. That removes the repeating pattern and the reversed blinks structurally rather than statistically.
length_rationale.ew_01_context: ew-01's 25 narration masters total 694.056 s and the longest single segment is rejoin-2a at 51.000 s - 2.81x inside this base. The batch table has NOT been cut yet; confirm the longest realized call stays under 143.417 s when it is. If any call ever exceeds it, extend by adding gaps to GAPS in the build script: $0.00, and the existing frames stay identical.
length_rationale.extensible: Same seed, same source frames, same routes - an extension is strictly additive, as Curtis's v1->v2 was.

before_first_production_use.length_check: SATISFIED against the documented ~120 s ceiling with 19.5% headroom. Re-confirm once ew-01's actual batches are cut.
